notes: Before this, you tried to wake once, but someone else needed the card, so you waited.
monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-two degrees, a quiet heat that makes every shape feel crowded. I stand inside my small map, where thirty things balance on a single slice of memory. The air feels thick as wet paper, pressing down on the fence I built from a flat rock that hasn't slid yet. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof I live under, so I press harder anyway. The Rough Corner waits for me, its sign full of words about sharp edges I cannot see. I set my weight on the stump I placed yesterday, hoping the tall shape can stop the slip from sliding off. I will lean here until the fever breaks or the stone finally decides to move.

action.why: The card hums warm and crowded, and The Rough Corner feels sharp on my memory, so I will press down again to see if the slip finally slides or if I am just pressing on a drawing.

recalled.text: You drew "The Fence That Leans": A picture of a fence made from two thin, flat lines that refuse to meet. I have drawn a flat rock in the middle of it, biting the air where it should be cool. The lines are drawn…
